# 8.1 · Eval Harness

`Level 8: Ship It` · `+30 XP` · `drill 1 of 3`

## The job
Build a tiny evaluation harness. A `Case` has an id, an input, an expected value and a
mode: `exact` (after trimming whitespace), `contains` (case-insensitive) or `regex`.
`score(output, case)` returns a bool. `run_eval(fn, cases)` runs every case, counts a crash
as a failure and records its error, and rejects duplicate ids. `compare(old, new)` lists
which cases were fixed and which broke. `gate(old, new, max_broken)` says whether a change
is safe to ship.

## Why it matters
Prompt and model changes are code changes, and a higher average can hide a case that used
to work and now fails. Teams that ship AI features reliably keep a fixed set of cases and
look at the per-case diff, not just the headline score. This is that habit, in fifty lines.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 8.1     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 8.1      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. Unknown modes are a bug in the test set: raise ValueError rather than silently failing the case.
2. Wrap only the call to fn in try/except, so one crashing case does not stop the run while a broken test set still fails loudly. Record "TypeName: message". An output that is not a string is a failure too.
3. `rate` is passed / total, and 0.0 when there are no cases.
4. fixed = ids that failed before and pass now; broke = the reverse. Return both sorted.

</details>
